title: Native retro remakes and application research
summary: Add seventeen qualified game and application research projects after reviewing 42 roots; record twenty-five deferrals and derivative cases.
notes: Root personally searched all six requested platform families and reviewed 42 pinned roots. Seventeen qualified game/reconstruction/application entries and twenty-five deferrals or duplicate-adjacent cases. No discovery worker used. Separate original-author remakes, source preservation, subsystem research and unfinished engines; do not infer fidelity from screenshots or a README claim. No upstream software executed. Pinned bytes are ephemeral local review material only; retained submission carries immutable proof identities without source excerpts.

sources.reason: Reconstructs only Snowball War, using recovered scripted arcs, team tables, scoring and asset formats. Original executable addresses anchor the behaviour spec and semantic Rust routines. Frame rate and PRNG are approximations; original shared engine, other events, menus and audio playback are outside completed scope.

Author preserved circa-1997 Amiga HDD source with named game loop, planet transition, animation and joystick routines. Single-planet remake; missing logic/graphics, title glitches and unclean exit are explicitly documented.

Substantial Delphi remake with dedicated game loop, pursuit/patrol/investigation ant AI and map editor. Includes a Zombie Zombie map repurposed for ants; Windows/OpenGL presentation is a remake, not original Z80 recovery.
Defold remake of Peace/Testaware Paragon. Board and match modules implement glyph placement, scoring, player turns, swaps and marathon options with separate AI.

Python/Pygame recreation of CPC Roland on the Ropes/Fred, with colour and green-screen modes, player movement, ropes and hazards. README explicitly limits it to one screen; art is screenshot-derived or redrawn and sounds are replacements.

Vimclair BASIC source credits partial reuse of Ian Andrew original Mined-Out code and graphics, with mine placement, trail/replay, rescue and multilingual UI. TODO describes deliberate mine/nest and scoring changes; this is a reinterpretation.

Java semantic remake of William Soleau Mice Men with explicit column shifts, mouse movement/escape, board analysis and computer players. README says publication has original-author permission. Revised difficulty and editable multiple saves are modern changes.

From-scratch canvas remake with tank digging, projectiles, shields/energy and bases. Replaces original local split-screen with online multiplayer. Author lists missing dirt-speed/shooting interaction, edge boulders and different explosion spread.

Ground-up Digger port using C64 multicolour character mode and sprite animation. Monster source directly controls VIC sprite registers and implements enemy spawning/movement. Author documents recreated graphics and occasional gameplay shortcuts.

Semantic Rust engine for Magic Carpet, Hidden Worlds and Magic Carpet 2. Original formats feed a deterministic simulation and new wgpu renderer. Spell tables preserve references to original/decompiled routines. Upstream claims per-tick retail-recording conformance, not binary-identical executable reconstruction; rendering/audio and redesigned multiplayer are outside exactness.

Semantic C++ remake includes maze rooms, enemy/base objectives, ship thrust/gravity/fuel/shields, projectiles, game-over/win states and saves. Source exposes recreated gameplay rather than a CPU interpreter; original physics/data equivalence is not established.

Version 0.1 semantic remake has track panels, ship acceleration/thrust/gravity and collision geometry. The source is a modern 3D implementation, not a translation of original DOS instructions; original level coverage is unverified.

Browser recreation includes player fuse placement, gas/fire spread, gas-can explosions and wall-destruction scoring. Source is incomplete/rough: the nested explosion call omits the level argument required by its function signature.
Early Godot vehicle/track prototype; source and README do not establish original Stunt Car Racer physics, campaign or AI reconstruction.
New TypeScript 3D racing implementation with replacement cars; inspected geometry and credits do not establish original Super Cars II simulation recovery.
Small TypeScript game scaffold intended to reproduce a first level; current public root lacks substantial gameplay implementation.
Useful reverse-engineered Atari ST audio-cartridge PCB, but hardware rather than game/application software in this pass.
Unity driving and city prototype with new vehicle/traffic implementation; original mission logic and numerical behaviour reconstruction not established.
README-only placeholder in the inspected tree; no Python Filemaster implementation available.
HTML5 sprite movement and map-editing prototype; squad combat, objectives and original mission logic not established.
Atari ST cartridge hardware reverse engineering; outside this game/application-source pass.
Elite-inspired modern game with generated universe; inspected delivery contains browser/framework assets and new rendering rather than documented original-code recovery.
Windows eSheep raw tool-generated listing and extracted assets, with author explicitly unable to interpret assembly; outside requested source platforms and insufficient semantic reconstruction.
COM disassembly experiment/tool, not a specific restored game or application; hold for tooling-focused discovery.

source_updates.reason: Pygame hex-map remake includes human/computer turns, unit actions and a map editor. FINdecoder inspects original file headers and tile/unit bytes, but is exploratory: its script exits before later decoding experiments. Do not describe it as a complete validated original-map decoder.

Open-source remake of DOS Sherlock logic puzzle, with 6-by-6 deduction, relational hints, saves, rules browser and themed/localised resources. Game source uses SDL widgets, hints and timers; no original DOS-code recovery claimed.

Annotated subsystem reconstruction combines matching historic source and researched exact modules. WildDOS kernel source names FAT32 state and driver API, with boundary ASSERTs in BOOT. Some exact Hrust-packed driver blocks remain binary resources because available recompression differs.

Research notes explain QBASIC parsing, generated grammar/opcode tables, coercion and interpreter execution, with POKE and screen-fill investigations. This repository contains notes and patch material, not the complete compiler/interpreter source.

Original Z80 runs inside a CPC emulator with replacement renderers. Original-format tools are useful, but game-specific emulation is deferred under the user's preference rather than listed as a native engine reconstruction.
Public tree contains data, manual and bug notes but no engine source despite partial-open-source wording; do not treat it as a public complete reconstruction.
LÖVE Lua movement/collision preview; original Exile world simulation, entities and puzzle reconstruction not established.
Modern redesign with procedural caves, new presentation and altered rules, not original binary/data reconstruction in this pass.

Native CPC source found for already tracked harrier-attack-reloaded-cpc, whose canonical site is cp-soft.itch.io/harrier-attack-reloaded. RASM/Plus cartridge source documents modifications to original Harrier Attack; avoid duplicate project.
Public tree contains team/language data and a screenshot, not game-engine source. Hold rather than infer source availability from the title.
Playable engine scaffold explicitly leaves AP costs, damage/accuracy, mission timer and AI as SOURCE_REQUIRED; historical controls alone do not establish game reconstruction.
Harfang scene/camera prototype; inspected main loop does not establish original CPC gameplay reconstruction.
Release/download-oriented repository and beta redesign plan; no inspectable engine source established from the public tree.
Already tracked at its canonical Codeberg repository; GitHub now redirects readers there. Avoid duplicate moved-upstream listing.
README explicitly says cut-down DOS emulation, not decompilation; retain as game-specific-emulation deferral.
Title/demo-scroller presentation recreation, not the Shadow of the Beast gameplay engine.

Matching assembly feeds instruction-by-instruction JavaScript preserving registers, flags and segmented memory, with new HD observer renderer. Defer game-specific emulation/static register translation rather than describe as semantic engine rewrite.
Raylib/Python tile/track-placement prototype and Train state class; moving train dispatch and original game loop are not established.
